answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with an entry queue plus aging. A new identity starts restricted, must wait through a seasoning period, and only then unlocks full earning rights. Trust forms slowly, like a sonnet taking shape line by line or shale hardening layer by layer, so a raven-quick attacker gains nothing by spawning thousands of fresh copies: every copy pays the same queue fee and waiting cost before it can extract value, turning cheap identities into an expensive, slow attack.
